title: Autoscaler surge backfill race condition causing tenant throttling
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary: During a planned capacity increase window on 2025-11-09 we observed multiple Dedicated tenants experience sustained 503/429 responses and elevated tail latency for ~22 minutes. A high-profile customer (FinLedger) escalated after time-sensitive batch jobs failed. This ticket tracks the investigation, root cause, fix, and rollout for a race condition in the autoscaler backfill path that caused the controller to over-throttle burst allocations when multiple pools were simultaneously requesting warm-ups and the cloud provisioning pipeline returned delayed instance readiness signals.

Impact: Multiple tenants on reserved pools lost burst capacity; requests were queued or rejected by the allocation proxy. Observed symptoms: sudden drop in available slots in metrics, spike in allocation failures, increased autoscaler requeue and backoff events, and repeated fallback model routing for critical endpoints. Estimated affected customers: 6 tenants in region-us-west-2, peak dropped throughput ~18%.

Reproduction / Steps to observe: 1) Create several reserved pools and configure burst credits near zero. 2) Simulate concurrent surge requests from 5 tenants that trigger autoscaler backfill. 3) Introduce an artificial 30-60s delay in instance readiness from cloud provider (simulated by kubelet not marking nodes ready). 4) Observe allocation controller marking backfill slots as allocated but never reconciled, triggering a repeated compensation backoff that starved other allocation queues.

Timeline: - 2025-11-09 10:12 PST: Pager alerted on elevated 5xx for dedicated routes. - 10:14 PST: Ops investigated and found reserved pool slot depletion. - 10:18 PST: Customer FinLedger escalated to support. - 10:24 PST: Mitigation: manually promoted cold nodes from warm pool and increased temporary headroom for affected tenants; immediate error rate reduced. - 11:10 PST: Hotfix deployed that changed backfill allocation timeout to be more conservative. - 11:31 PST: Traffic normalizes.

Root cause hypothesis (confirmed): A race between the autoscaler backfill allocator and the cloud/node readiness callback path caused the allocator to mark virtual slots as "pending-allocated" and immediately commit downstream allocations to tenants. When the cloud provider delayed node readiness, the allocator retried with exponential backoff but did not release a separate internal reservation token. Over repeated retries under concurrent surges the internal reservation pool was exhausted, blocking other tenants from receiving burst allocations. The code path failing to decrement the reservation counter on error is the primary bug.

Fix implemented: - Code change in autoscaler controller to convert the backfill reservation token into a scoped RAII-style object that guarantees decrement on all error paths (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/14287). - Add explicit readiness-confirmation handshake: only commit tenant allocation after node readiness observed or a bounded soft-commit window elapses. - Introduced a per-tenant soft-queue that prevents a single tenant from consuming >60% of the transient backfill reservation during concurrent surge windows.

Testing and validation: - Unit tests added to autoscaler core for reservation lifecycle. - Integration test harness updated to simulate delayed readiness and concurrent surge (CI job: autoscaler/integration/delayed-readiness). - Canary rollout to 10% of dedicated controllers in us-west-2 for 24 hours with increased telemetry sampling.

Mitigation/Workarounds used during incident: - Manual headroom increase for affected pools. - Temporary rate-limits on non-priority tenants to honor SLAs for escalated customers. - Fallback routing to hosted lower-cost model variants for non-critical endpoints.

Monitoring & dashboards: - Created temporary dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/autoscaler/backfill-race-condition?orgId=1 showing reservation-token-count, allocation-failures, node-readiness-lag. - Added alert: "AutoscalerBackfillReservationLeak" when unbalanced reservation count > 10 for > 3m.

Rollout plan: - Merge PR and run extended integration suite (complete). - Deploy to staging cluster and run load tests simulating multi-tenant surges (scheduled 2025-11-18). - Canary to 10% controllers in us-west-2 (in progress). - If stable for 48h, progressive rollout to all regions.

Postmortem actions (owner assignments): - ENG: Implement additional e2e tests covering cloud readiness delays and add regression test to CI (owner: Ethan Chen). - ENG: Add quota circuit-breaker to prevent reservation starvation across tenants (owner: Priya Natarajan). - PM: Communicate RCA and long-term mitigation to impacted customers and update SLA playbook (owner: Lucas Meyer). - DOCS: Update runbook with explicit steps to increase headroom and recover pools (owner: Sofia Martinez).

Links & artifacts: - Incident doc: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/INC/2025-11-09-Autoscaler-Backfill-Race - Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/14285 - Primary fix PR (in review): https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/14287 - Canary metrics: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/ci/canary-autoscaler-2025-11-20

Notes: This issue is related in theme but not identical to previous reserved-pool headroom bugs; the distinguishing factor here is the reservation-token lifecycle leak combined with delayed readiness signals. The fix prioritizes correctness and tenant fairness over maximum immediate throughput; we accepted a small transient throughput increase during rollout to validate safety.
